# 9. Trust and Security Model

Security in O-CPS is layered: cryptographic identity provides authentication and non-repudiation; pseudonymity limits long-term correlation; continuous attestation provides integrity signals; misbehavior detection produces consensus-grounded trust scores; and revocation removes compromised or misbehaving participants from the population.

## 9.1 Identity and Pseudonymous Certificates

### 9.1.1 Certificate Structure

Every O-CPS participant holds a pool of short-lived pseudonym certificates, each bound to an ECDSA P-256 signing key. Pseudonym certificates MUST conform to the profile of IEEE 1609.2.1 (SCMS) or ETSI TS 102 941 (C-ITS). Each certificate carries the Permissions Service Specific Permissions (PSSP) required for the message classes the participant is entitled to transmit; a participant unable to emit a given class MUST NOT be issued a certificate that permits it.

### 9.1.2 Rotation

Certificates MUST be rotated at least every 5 minutes during active operation, and a fresh certificate MUST be selected on every instance of the following events: entering a new geographic cell (as defined by the SCMS geographic region partition), emerging from a GNSS-denied environment, or power-cycle. Butterfly key expansion per IEEE 1609.2.1 SHOULD be used so that pseudonyms within an epoch are not linkable without possession of the CA’s linkage keys.

### 9.1.3 Enrollment

Initial enrollment MUST require proof of possession of a hardware root of trust. The vehicle’s HSM generates the enrollment keypair; the public key is attested by a manufacturer-issued device certificate; the enrollment certificate authority binds the device attestation to an enrollment identity that is NEVER transmitted over the air during normal operation. Only pseudonym certificates travel on the wire.

## 9.2 Continuous Attestation

Static trust anchors (a valid certificate at session start) do not answer the question of whether a participant’s current software and sensor state merits the authority implicit in its messages. O-CPS addresses this with continuous attestation.

A conforming participant emits an Attestation message at least every 10 seconds while actively transmitting PerceptionSummary. The attestation is an HSM- or TPM-signed statement of: (a) the fingerprint of the currently-loaded O-CPS software; (b) the fingerprint of the currently-loaded vehicle perception software; (c) the boot-time attestation of the compute platform; and (d) a summary of the health of each sensor modality.

Peers maintain a per-sender attestation record with a lifetime of 30 seconds. Absence of a current attestation downgrades the sender’s trust weight to ADVISORY (see §12). A currently-valid attestation whose fingerprints match a known-revoked software build also downgrades the sender, and triggers a misbehavior report.

## 9.3 Misbehavior Detection

Misbehavior in O-CPS is defined as any pattern of transmitted messages that is internally inconsistent, inconsistent with the laws of physics, or inconsistent with the consensus of peers and local sensors. Each of these is detectable:

- **Internal inconsistency: **a sender reports its own pose at (x,y,z), then reports perceived objects at relative positions that, when transformed to world coordinates, place them on top of its own pose.
- **Physical implausibility: **a sender reports a velocity or acceleration in excess of vehicle-class limits, or reports poses that imply instantaneous teleportation.
- **Consensus deviation: **a sender repeatedly reports objects in positions where no other sender in the same area reports any object, and the receiver’s own sensors do not corroborate.
- **Attestation anomaly: **a sender produces valid pseudonym certificates but cannot produce current attestation, or attestation fingerprints correspond to a revoked software build.

A conforming implementation MUST run all four classes of detector continuously on all received messages and MUST emit a Misbehavior Report over the cellular control-plane interface to the appropriate Misbehavior Authority when any detector fires above its threshold. Misbehavior Reports are OUT of the safety-critical loop; they do not affect real-time fusion. Real-time response is limited to trust-weight de-rating (§12.3).

## 9.4 Revocation

The SCMS or C-ITS PKI operates a Certificate Revocation List (CRL) and a linkage-based revocation mechanism per IEEE 1609.2.1. O-CPS participants MUST ingest the current CRL at least once per day while connectivity permits, and MUST refuse to honor messages signed by revoked certificates. Participants whose own enrollment certificate is revoked MUST cease all O-CPS transmission within 60 seconds of ingesting the revocation.
